content.title: About
content.content: Popcorn chips are crunchy snacks made from whole popcorn kernels that are toasted until golden and then coated with a variety of flavor blends. Unlike traditional potato chips, they contain less fat and have a lighter texture while delivering a bold taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Popcorn is the only grain that “pops” when heated due to internal steam pressure.
Popcorn chips first appeared in the United States in the early 2000s as a healthier alternative to greasy snacks.
Different flavors are achieved with spices, dry dairy mixes, cheese powders, and natural flavor extracts.
They are often marketed as a lower‑calorie snack, containing up to 30 % fewer calories than comparable potato chips.
In some markets they are sold in “cube” packets, where each piece is a small square.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with most potato chips, popcorn chips can contain as little as 5 %–10 % fat, making them a lighter snack option.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain popcorn provides dietary fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Polysaccharides and small amounts of polyphenols in popcorn help combat free radicals.

items.title: Better glycemic response
items.content: The starch in popcorn has a lower glycemic index than potato, contributing to more stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Popcorn supplies thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Allergy to flavorings
items.content: Some seasoning blends may contain dairy or soy ingredients that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salty varieties can contain up to 400 mg of sodium per 30 g serving, which should be considered by those with hypertension.

items.title: Caloric intake if over‑consumed
items.content: Although lower in fat, eating large amounts still adds up in calories.

items.title: Choking hazard for young children
items.content: The crunchy pieces can pose a choking risk for small kids.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Popcorn chips are perfect as a stand‑alone snack, tossed into salads, used as a crunchy topping for soups, or paired with dips. They make a great accompaniment to beer or a movie night.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the package in a cool, dry place and reseal tightly after opening. For longer storage, transfer to an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption, which can make the chips soggy.
